summary: Echoes Across the Void is an interactive, scroll-driven story website for school-age kids and curious teens. It tells the stories of ten NASA machines left on the Moon and Mars, from Surveyor 3 and the Apollo rovers to Viking, Spirit, Opportunity, InSight and the Ingenuity helicopter. Each machine gets a chapter with real mission facts, a count-up stat showing how far it outlived its plan, and a short imagined “last words” line, labeled as imagined. It answers the “Abandoned but not Forgotten” challenge by turning dusty mission archives into something young people want to read, and shows that these machines still matter: they proved what is possible and showed where to go next. The site opens on a single title and reveals the story as you scroll, ending with a “ping the void” interaction.
details: Echoes Across the Void is a single-page website that works like a short film. It opens on the title alone, and the story arrives as you scroll: a prologue, then ten chapters (3 on the Moon, 7 on Mars), then a finale where visitors “ping” the Moon or Mars and see how long a reply really takes. Each chapter has an animated signal scope, a count-up stat, a planned-versus-actual lifespan bar, three facts and a typewriter “last words” line. Mission dates, lifespans and facts come from NASA mission archives. The goal is to make space history approachable for kids with no science background, and to show that the machines left behind still matter. We built it with HTML, CSS, JavaScript and canvas (starfield and scroll effects), with original line-art icons drawn in code. We chose a dark, cinematic, poetic style with big modern type so it feels like a story, not a fact sheet. It is mobile-friendly and has a reduced-motion mode. We used Claude (Anthropic) to help write code, draft story copy and draw the icons, and the site footer says so.
